dedupe_keys.name: i 70 truck platooning project between columbus and indianapolis ohio and indiana dots 2025

description: A multi-year, 8.8 million dollar deployment by the Ohio and Indiana departments of transportation of two partially automated, platooning tractor-trailers on Interstate 70 between Columbus and Indianapolis. Coverage: one interstate freight corridor, with trucks hauling real loads for EASE Logistics customers since April 2025 to test the technology in Midwestern weather. Methods: Kratos Defense equipment electronically links the trucks so the lead driver controls the speed and direction of the second, which steers, accelerates and brakes automatically; professional drivers stay in both cabs. Outcome: an ODOT update on 11 August 2025 reported more than 2,700 miles in platooning mode and nearly 50 deliveries with better fuel efficiency; further deployments were to be tendered. Format and access: free news reports quoting ODOT; no technical evaluation was read. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: early results from a small pilot, reported by the agencies and trade press. Useful for capacity planning and network flow studies of automated freight corridors and their weather limits. It relates to the FHWA truck platooning early deployment case and the Freight Analysis Framework in the catalogue.
